Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. JUN Z ATTY. JOY RANDOLF N. TORRE-CARION Secretary to the Sanggunian Murcia, Negros Occidental Dear Atty. Torrecarion: 96 s. 2010 This has reference to your earlier letter asking the Department's legal opinion on the following issues, to wit: "1) Whether or not the minutes Of the sanggunian cannot be considered as public records and cannot therefore be furnished to the interested requesting party? and 2) Whether or not the appointing authority of the Secretary to the Sanggunian is the local chief executive?" In reply to your first query, may we invite your attention to the following provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), thus; "SECTION 52. sessions.— (e) Each sanggunian shall keep a journal and record of its proceedings which may be published upon resolution of the sanggunian concerned. " "SECTION 469. Qual if i cations , Duties . xxx xxx Power S and (c) The secretary to the sanggunian shall take charge of the office of the secretary to the sanggunian and shall: (1) Attend meetings of the sanggunian and keep a journal of its proceedings; (2) Keep the seal of the local government unit and affix the same with his signature to all ordinances, resolutions, and other official acts of the sanggunian and present the same to the presiding officer for his signature; (5) Furnish, upon request of any interested party, certified copies of records of public character in

his custody, upon payment to the treasurer of such fees as may be prescribed by ordinance; xxx -2- Based on the aforequoted provisions, the journal and record of proceedings of each sanggunian shall be kept by the secretary to the sanggunian. Said journal may be published upon resolution of the sanggunian concerned. Let it be noted that Section 52 (e) used the word "may" vis-å-vis the publication of the same. The word "may" is generally permissive only and operates to confer discretion. If there is no publication of the journal due, for example, to the failure of the sanggunian to issue a resolution to that effect as required under Section 52 (e) of the Code, we are of the view that the secretary to the sanggunian may nevertheless furnish a copy of the minutes of the sanggunian to any interested party, upon the latter's prior request and upon payment of the required fees, pursuant to Section 469 (c) (5) of the Local Government Code of 1991. The journal or minutes of the proceedings are considered public records as contemplated under Section 469 (c) (5) of the Code. In De los Reyes vs. Sandiganbayan and the People of the Philippines, G.R. No. 121215, November 13, 1997, minutes of the meetings are the official repository of what actually transpired in every proceeding. Along this line, Section 7, Article III of the 1987 Constitution provides and we quote: "Section 7. The right of the people to information on matters of public concern shall be recognized. Access to official records, and to documents, and papers pertaining to official acts, transactions, or decisions, as well as to government research date used as basis for policy development, shall be afforded the citizen, subject to such limitations as may be provided by law." Anent your second query, please be informed that we already answered a similar query in DILG Opinion No. 110, series of 2004. In the said legal opinion, we opined that the sanggunian secretary is appointed by the local vice- chief executive. A photocopy of the aforesaid DILG Opinion is hereto attached for your ready perusal. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: J Copy furnished: Regional Director Evelyn A. DE QUIROS Sangguniang Panlalawigan Secretary Provincial Capitol Building Virac, Catanduanes Dear Mr. de Quiros: 'Ibis refers to your letter-request for this Department's legal opinion on whether or not the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, through a Resolution duly passed, can relieve you from performing your duties as the Sanggunian Secretary. Your query anchored on the following antecedents which this Depaltment states briefly. Thus: On 21 September 2004, you were requested by "Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Rosemarie Zafe to submit to her and the rest of the Board a copy of the Minutes of the 13 March 2004 special session; On the same occasion, you informed SP Member Zafe that you are not in possession of the said Minutes as you were not the Sanggunian Secretary on that day, as it was fonner SI' Member dei Valle who is now the Vice-Mayor of' San Andres, Catanduanes, who acted as the Temporary Secretary on the 13 March 2004 special session. 'Illat despite your repeated requests for Vice-Mayor del Valle to submit the copy of the Minutes on the 13 March 2004 special session, in compliance with the request of SP Member Za(e, Vice-Mayor del Valle has yet to respond to you. On 07 December 2004, after having informed t.he Sangguniang Panlalawigan that Mr. del Valle has not yet responded to your letters anent SP Mernber Zafe's earlier request, SY Member Ccigar Tapel filed a Resolution excusing you of your functions to take down the Minutes during [he sessions for failure to produce the subject Minutes being requested until such time that lhe latter is submitted. .4

-2- Hence, your query. We reply to your query in the negative. Let it be noted that a Sanggunian Secretauy is a career official who is appointed by the Local Vice-Chief Executive. Since the power to appoint carries with it the power to supervise and discipline, save in certain cases, then, only Lhe Vice-Governor or Vice-Mayor can "excuse" or "relieve" the Sanggunian Secretauy whom the [ormer has appointed, but only upon the existence of a just cause. Sanggunian Secretaries are not confidential employees who may be emoved due to loss of confidence by the appointing authority, rather, they ar.e permanent career officials who may only be removed after a finding of administrative guilt against them by the proper authority. No Sanggunian Resolution "excusing" or "relieving" its secretary from performing the latter's functions can xeve.r hold legal ground as the former does not have jurisdiction over the person or even any supposed infraction that may have been committed by the secretary. The action of your Sanggunian in relieving you from your duties is, therefore, without legal basis, hence, produces no effect. Such being the case, perfonnance of your functions as Sangguniang Secretary must continue. May it be noted further that an officer or employee of the Civil Service may only be suspended or disrnissed for cause provided by law, per no less than Section 2 (3), Article IX-B oi the 1987 Constitution. We are thus in a quandary on what legal basis was relied upon by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Catanduanes in "excusing" or "relieving" you from your duties as Secretary. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Ve truly yours, AN El_ T.
